notes:
DIMENSION: Supabase, sign-in and multi-company parity with Boxlytics and Solarlytics, under the owner's rule.
The owner's rule: no Google or other social sign-in, no magic link, no self-signup. Sign-in is by preassigned accounts only, as in solarlytics-backend.

SOURCES READ
- Boxlytics web (boxlytics-main):
  - SUPABASE_SETUP.md, AUTHENTICATION_IMPLEMENTATION.md, both .env.example files, supabase/config.toml and supabase/README.md;
  - supabase/functions: send-invite (Resend email template), founder-admin with SETUP.md, _shared/founder-auth.ts;
  - migrations 001-012 and db/;
  - src/services: supabase.client.ts, auth.service.ts; the App.tsx routes;
  - BACKEND_WIRING_CONTRACT.md.
  - There is no middleware.js: it is a Vite SPA.
- Boxlytics backend: core/security.py (one shared X-API-Key), the env examples, docker-compose, Dockerfile, run_server.py, docs/TENANCY_BOUNDARY.md.
- Solarlytics backend (main c853130):
  - supabase/README.md, sql/solar_000_preflight.sql, migrations/solar_001_accounts_and_companies.sql and solar_001_rollback.sql;
  - identity, platform, companies, auth, founder, mfa, routes_local, routes_founder, store_founder, store_members, and api.py's users routes;
  - DESIGN_LOG's sign-in section and docs/split.
- Solarlytics web (d582a5f): services/supabase.client.ts, auth.service.ts, localauth.service.ts, pages/auth/{Login, ResetPassword, NotSetUp}.tsx, .env.example.
- Gridlytics: every module named in the task; api.py users, auth state and mounting; features/auth/*; app/env.ts; .env.example; source-rules.test.ts; the org pages; plan Parts 2, 10, 11 and the tracker; U1 and U2; DESIGN_LOG; HANDOFF; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

Diffing after the solarlytics→gridlytics rename:
- identity, companies, platform, founder, mfa, routes_local and routes_founder are byte-identical.
- auth changes only the roles and drops open mode.
- store_founder and store_members change only the counts and the legacy linking.
- The web's local-auth.service is a verbatim lift.

(1) CAPABILITY TABLE (Boxlytics | Solarlytics | Gridlytics)
- **Auth providers.** Boxlytics: Supabase email and password plus Google OAuth; open sign-up (/register, /auth/callback); a dummy "magic link" toast. Solarlytics: local email and password (PBKDF2), plus an optional supabase mode whose README checklist turns sign-ups, Google, every other provider and anonymous sign-in off; identity.verify refuses tokens whose amr lacks "password" or whose provider is not "email". Gridlytics: local mode, identical, with the same amr and provider check, but no checklist. DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED (owner's rule): Google, /auth/callback, sign-up and RegisterPage, magic link, OAuth consent-screen steps.
- **profiles and handle_new_user trigger.** Boxlytics: yes (001 §5.1, walks the Google metadata), plus touch_updated_at. Solarlytics: yes in solar_001 (supabase mode); the local `accounts` table otherwise. Gridlytics: local `accounts` only, no SQL. Finding: missing supabase/ folder.
- **Companies.** Boxlytics: self-created, verified by a super-admin, seat_limit, a force-pending trigger. Solarlytics: registry (enabled, seats, disabled_reason) made by the founder; the project's `companies` uses the same id. Gridlytics: registry as in Solarlytics.
- **Memberships.** Boxlytics: owner/admin/member and pending/active/suspended, one owner per company. Solarlytics: the same; local mode allows two owners for a hand-over. Gridlytics: the same as Solarlytics.
- **RLS.** Boxlytics: about 20 policies plus SECURITY DEFINER helpers on 6 tables. Solarlytics: 5 policies, REVOKE/GRANT, get_my_context and company_list_members. Gridlytics: none (no SQL); tenancy is enforced per request by companies.resolve, verified live.
- **Invites.** Boxlytics: company_invites, the send-invite edge function (Resend) and /invite/:token. Solarlytics: none ("no invitations"). Gridlytics: none, which matches Solarlytics. DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED.
- **Onboarding (intent, new company, join existing, pending and rejected screens, restart).** Boxlytics only. NOT PORTED (preassigned accounts).
- **Seats and tokens.** Boxlytics: seat_limit plus the 011 token economy (balance, ledger, spend_tokens, pricing). Solarlytics: seats plus commercial plans, no tokens. Gridlytics: seats only. Token economy NOT PORTED.
- **Super-admin and founder.** Boxlytics: profiles.is_super_admin plus the founder-admin edge function (sha256 password, TOTP, HMAC session, service role, impersonation, platform_settings flags such as signups_enabled, maintenance_mode and announcement, token grants). Solarlytics: founder console in the backend (PBKDF2 or sha256, TOTP with a replay guard, lockouts, audit). Gridlytics: identical to Solarlytics. NOT PORTED: is_super_admin, impersonation, feature flags, token grants.
- **Web environment variables.** Boxlytics: VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, VITE_API_KEY (a shared key in the bundle) and VITE_API_BASE_URL. Solarlytics: VITE_AUTH_MODE local|supabase, VITE_API_BASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. Gridlytics: VITE_API_BASE_URL and VITE_AUTH_MODE (enum "local" only). Finding.
- **Service-role key on the backend.** Boxlytics: edge functions and the dataset pipeline only. Solarlytics: SOLARLYTICS_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, used by the founder console, documented in .env.production.example and the README. Gridlytics: store_founder reads GRIDLYTICS_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, documented nowhere. Finding.
- **JWT verification.** Boxlytics FastAPI: none (shared key). Solarlytics: HS256 locally, or JWKS ES256/RS256 or the legacy HS256 secret; exp, iat, sub, aud and iss required. Gridlytics: identical. Live: alg none, a foreign HS256 key, a foreign ES256 key, garbage and a 9 KB token all give 401 token_invalid; a founder token used as a bearer gives 401; a user token on a founder route gives 401.
- **Session refresh.** Boxlytics: supabase-js auto-refresh. Solarlytics and Gridlytics: rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection. Live in Gridlytics: refresh after logout, after a password change and after a disable all give 401.
- **Password reset.** Boxlytics: resetPasswordForEmail to a /reset-password route that does not exist. Solarlytics: the founder sets the password; supabase mode adds a reset mail and the /reset-password page; the login page says "Ask us". Gridlytics: the founder only; the login page says "ask your company's administrator", who cannot. Finding.
- **Email templates.** Boxlytics: the Resend invite template plus Supabase's defaults. Solarlytics: a reset-template note (SMTP still missing). Gridlytics: none.
- **Storage buckets.** None in any of the three (Boxlytics src never calls supabase.storage).
- **Company switch.** Boxlytics: picks a default, with no switcher. Solarlytics and Gridlytics: an X-…-Company header, a per-tab choice, a chooser and a switch. Live in Gridlytics, all as designed:
  - a person in two companies gets 409 company_required without the header;
  - another company's id gets 403 not_a_member;
  - junk headers ('../../etc/passwd', SQL-like text, 5,000 characters) get 403 not_a_member;
  - an upper-case uuid is accepted;
  - a company switched off gives 403 company_disabled, and the request falls back to the only company still on;
  - another company's site gives 404;
  - the chooser and the menu switch work at 1440 and 375 (screenshots in supa-auth/shots).
- **Password rule.** Boxlytics: Supabase default. Solarlytics: 10-200 characters locally, 10-72 in supabase mode. Gridlytics: 10-200 and not only spaces (verified).
- **Lockout and rate limits.** Boxlytics: Supabase Auth's per-IP limits. Solarlytics and Gridlytics: 5 tries per (email, address) lock for 15 min; the public limit is 1,200 a minute per address. Finding.

(3) LIVE CHECKS THAT ARE FINE
- Disable gives 401 session_ended at once, both access and refresh.
- A suspended or pending membership is refused.
- A self password change ends every other session and keeps this one.
- Unknown emails and wrong passwords get the same sentence and code.
- The founder-console flows work (create a company with its owner; add an account to a second company).

Plan quality was not judged, and audit load affects none of these results.

NOT RE-RAISED (earlier reviewers already filed them; re-confirmed where noted)
- An access token keeps working after logout. Re-confirmed: s2 access after logout gives 200.
- The founder cannot clear a lockout.
- Founder-issued passwords are not one-time.
- The company role "Admin" maps to Viewer.
- A seatless member sees the wrong sentence.
- The lockout uses a shared "forwarded" bucket behind a proxy.
